entries.summary: Verified MessagingClient wraps SqsClient (not vice versa); watermill uses raw SqsClient only for receive to get ApproximateReceiveCount
entries.detail: PR #1127 reviewer asked why cloud-sdk MessagingClient and AWS v2 SqsClient coexist; user hypothesised SqsClient is a wrapper internally using MessagingClient. VERIFIED FROM CODE + JAR - the relationship is the REVERSE: cloud-sdk MessagingClient is the wrapper; its AWS impl com.inttra.mercury.cloudsdk.messaging.aws.impl.SqsMessagingClient (cloud-sdk-aws-1.0.28-SNAPSHOT) has `private final software.amazon.awssdk.services.sqs.SqsClient sqsClient`, constructor `SqsMessagingClient(SqsClient, MessageConverter<T>)`, and implements sendMessage/receiveMessages/deleteMessage by delegating to that internal SqsClient. In watermill: SQSClient (sender) uses cloud-sdk MessagingClient<String> via @Named amazonSQSForSender / MessagingClientFactory.createDefaultStringClient() for send/delete/getQueueAttributes; SQSListenerClient (receive) uses the RAW AWS v2 SqsClient directly via @Named amazonSQSForListener and requests messageSystemAttributeNames(APPROXIMATE_RECEIVE_COUNT), adapting each result to cloud-sdk QueueMessage<String> via SqsQueueMessage. They coexist because the cloud-sdk MessagingClient in 1.0.28 cannot request SQS system attributes (ApproximateReceiveCount) needed by the cargo-visibility retry/redelivery framework - documented as a temporary reach-around in 2026-07-30 doc section 9. So SqsClient is NOT a wrapper around MessagingClient; it is the raw SDK client used directly on the receive path only. PR link requires SSO (could not web-fetch); verified via source + javap.

CORRECTION to my earlier analysis: the reviewer means watermill SQSClient (the sender wrapper), NOT the raw AWS v2 SqsClient. So SQSClient IS a value-adding wrapper over MessagingClient (user's belief confirmed); not redundant. (2) PR-Agent bot flagged S3WorkspaceService.getMetaData stream leak - already ADDRESSED (try-with-resources + IOException catch present). (3) Bot PR Reviewer Guide score 92, no action.
